reason: Wording: the Dickinson Electronic Archives text of L330 (June 1869, to Higginson) reads verbatim “A Letter always feels to me like immortality because it is the mind alone without corporeal friend.” The capital L on Letter is Dickinson’s. The circulating variant “A letter always seemed to me like immortality” is the corrupt one (Todd’s 1894 text), not this; Johnson’s numbering and date agree. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, Dickinson at 2 of 3 (months 1 and 2), not banned. In scope, publishable, and the letter is itself a thank-you (it goes on to “Gratitude is the timid wealth of those who have nothing”), so it fits Gratitude and Mortality twice. Source 102 characters, leads with the name, no dash; Johnson named as editor (Theodora Ward was associate editor, which need not be in the byline). Tag Correspondence fits. Residual: the Harvard 1958 printed page was not opened; the archive transcription follows the manuscript and Johnson. Editor’s flag, not a refutation: the carry-in 06-poet-08 (Dickinson, I’m nobody!) is also fitted to November, and only one Dickinson may land in the month; landing both would also exceed her cap of three.
